With the consent of the learned counsel for the parties the appeal is heard finally.

2. This present appeal under Section 30 of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 is filed being aggrieved by the award dated 14.01.2015 passed by the Learned Commissioner for Employees Compensation-cum-Labour Court, Raipur (CG) in Case No. 166/W.C.Act/2007/Fatal.

3. Vide the said impugned award, the learned Commissioner has allowed the claim application of the appellants-claimants and has awarded a compensation of an amount of Rs. 1,74,605/- to be paid within a period of two months.

4. In this appeal, the following substantial question of law is involved:
Smt. Saraswati Devi vs Sunil Steel Industries on 18 August, 2023

Grievance of the appellants-claimants who are the widow and children of the deceased, is that the Commissioner has failed to provide the interest and penalty on the awarded amount from the date of accident which the claimants are entitled for in view of the provisions of Section 4A of the Workmen's Compensation Act.

The learned Commissioner, after due appreciation of evidence on record, decided the issues No. 3 & 8 in favour of the appellants-claimants and the respondent No.3/insurance Company was held liable to pay the compensation.

6. Learned counsel for the appellants-claimants submits that though the award was passed by the Commissioner on account of death of deceased Ashok Singh but while awarding compensation, no interest and penalty was directed to be paid on the awarded amount which is contrary to sub section 3 of Section 4 (A) of the Employees Compensation Act therefore, the substantial question of law may be answered in favour of the appellants- claimants.

Likewise, the Commissioner has also failed to provide the interest and penalty on the awarded amount from the date of accident which the claimants are otherwise entitled for in view of the provisions of Section 4 A of the Workmen's Compensation Act.

7. Learned counsel for the respondent No.1 opposing the appeal submits that the appeal has been filed with a delay of about nine months after passing of the award dated 14.01.2015 and it has not been explained properly therefore, the award passed by the Commissioner is just and reasonable and does not warrant any interference.
8.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ved Prakash Garg (supra) held in Paragraph 19 after dealing with the said issue while answering the issue, has held as under:
19.
As a result of the aforesaid discussion it must be held that the question posed for our consideration must be answered partly in the affirmative and partly in the negative.

In other words the insurance company will be liable to meet the claim for compensation along with interest as imposed on the insured employer the Workmen's Commissioner under the Compensation Act on the conjoint operation of Section 3 and Section Act on the Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:21378 conjoint operation of Section 3 and Section 4A sub- additional amount of compensation y way of penalty imposed on the insured employer by the Workmen's Commissioner under Section 4(3) (b) is concerned, however, the insurance company would not remain liable to reimburse the said claim and it would be the liability of the insured employer alone.
10.The aforesaid principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the said case still holds fit and recently again in the case of Kamla Chaturvedi (supra), has reiterated the aforesaid principle in paragraph 7 & 8, held as under:
7.

In Ved Prakash Garg v. Premi Devi and others [1997(8) SCC 1] this court observed that the Insurance Company is liable to pay not only the principal amount of compensation payable by the insurer employer but also interest thereon if ordered by the Commissioner to be paid by the insured, employee.

however, held that it was the liability of the insured employer alone in respect of additional amount of compensation by way of penalty under Section 4(A)(3)(b) of the Act.

sentences.text: A contract of Insurance is governed by the provisions of the Insurance Act, 1938 (in short the `Insurance Act'), unless the said contract is governed by the provisions of a statute.
The parties are free to enter into a contract as per their own volition.
The Act does not contain a provision like Section 148 of the MV Act where a statute does not provide for a compulsory insurance or accident thereof.
The parties are free to choose their terms of contract.
In that view of the matter contracting out so far as the reimbursement of amount of interest is concerned is not prohibited by a statute."
This position have been reiterated in P.J. Narayan v. Union of India and others [2006 (5) SCC 200].

entities.text: P.J. Narayan v. Union of India and others [2006 (5) SCC 200
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the instant case the position is different.
The accident in question arose on account of vehicular accident and provisions of MV Act are clearly applicable.

We have gone through the policy of Neutral Citation 2023:CGHC:21378 insurance and we find that no such exception as was the case in New India Assurance Co.'s case was stipulated in the policy of insurance.
Therefore, the Insurance Company is liable to pay the interest.

11. In view of the aforesaid two categorical judgments on the issue involved in the present appeal,
the finding given by the learned Commissioner by not awarding the interest on the amount of compensation is bad in the eye of law and therefore the substantial question of law is answered in affirmative.
The respondent No.3/Insurance Company is held liable to pay interest at rate of 12% on the awarded amount i.e. Rs. 1,74,605/- from the date of accident i.e. on 19.10.2005 till the deposit ismade.
Rest of the conditions of the impugned award shall remain intact.
Copy of this order may be sent to the appellant No.1-claimant for information.
No order as to cost.
